# Note Keeper — Specification

## Summary

Note Keeper is a web application for individuals to capture, organize, search, and revisit notes, as described in the Note Keeper product requirements document. This specification covers the MVP release: authentication, note creation and editing with auto-saved and sanitized rich text, a notes dashboard, nested folders, tags, full-text search, pinning, archive/trash with recovery, checklists, attachments, version history, and export/import.

The PRD does not mandate a technology stack or repository layout. The declared artifacts below assume one plausible structure — a TypeScript HTTP API under `server/` and a React client under `client/` — as a basis for delivery, not as a design mandate; this assumption should be confirmed rather than treated as decided. Google sign-in is named only as a future enhancement in the PRD, so no criterion below requires it, and it is listed as out of scope.

Native offline-first mobile apps, full team collaboration and workspace administration, advanced document layout, full project-management features, and public publishing are explicit PRD non-goals and are excluded below.

Where the PRD gives an illustrative number rather than a fixed rule (the attachment file-size limit, and the trash/version retention windows), the criteria below require a documented, enforced limit or window rather than fixing it at the PRD's example value.

The PRD states several expectations as soft guidance ("should") rather than as a specific, independently testable obligation for a given artifact: regular backups with a restoration procedure, sub-200ms UI responsiveness "where network conditions allow," and support for "current versions" of major browsers. These are not translated into acceptance criteria below, since none of them names a fixed, checkable threshold; they remain open operational expectations for the design or operator to make concrete, not decisions this specification invents on the PRD's behalf.

This specification also leaves three security-relevant decisions open rather than inventing obligations the PRD does not state: access-control treatment for the full-collection export archive (which aggregates a user's entire note and attachment collection into one higher-value target), content-type and content-disposition handling for non-image attachment downloads, and password-reset token security properties (expiration, single-use enforcement, rate limiting). These are named again under Out of scope.

On self-review, AC-020 originally combined the functional search obligation with a numeric performance threshold; these are now separated into AC-020 and AC-058 so that a failure of either can be traced independently. AC-057 was added to cover the Trash view's listing behavior, which the original acceptance criteria left implicit despite `client/src/components/TrashView.tsx` being a declared artifact. Other compound criteria (AC-006, AC-009, AC-018, AC-034) were deliberately left bundled, matching how the PRD states each as a single feature bullet rather than as separately obligated sub-behaviors; further decomposition was not applied so as not to manufacture finer-grained obligations than the PRD draws.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-001: A visitor can register an account with email and password, sign in, sign out, and request a password reset.
- AC-002: A user who has requested a password reset can complete it by submitting the reset token or link with a new password, and can then sign in with the new password.
- AC-003: Each user can access only their own notes, folders, tags, attachments, and preferences; a request for another user's notes, folders, tags, attachments, or preferences is rejected.
- AC-004: Users can create a note from a prominent "New note" action, and the editor opens with the cursor focused in the title or body field.
- AC-005: A note supports a title, body content, folder assignment, tags, pinned state, archived state, checklist items, and creation/update timestamps.
- AC-006: The note editor supports headings, bold, italic, bulleted lists, numbered lists, checklists, links, block quotes, and code blocks.
- AC-007: Edits to a note are auto-saved after a debounce interval of 500-1,000 milliseconds after typing stops, without a manual save action.
- AC-008: The editor displays a visible save-state indicator showing Saving, Saved, Offline, or Unable to save.
- AC-009: Rich-text content is sanitized server-side against a fixed allow-list of tags and attributes matching the supported formatting before storage and before rendering, stripping disallowed tags, attributes, inline event handlers, and script content rather than escaping them.
- AC-010: Link and image URLs in rich-text content are restricted to the http, https, and mailto schemes during sanitization; a URL using any other scheme, including javascript: and data:, is rejected.
- AC-011: The dashboard displays recent notes, pinned notes, and quick-access controls including a "New note" action.
- AC-012: Notes can be sorted by last-updated date, creation date, title, or pinned status.
- AC-013: Each note card or row shows title, content preview, tags, folder, and last-updated timestamp.
- AC-014: The dashboard shows an empty state that guides a new user to create their first note when they have none.
- AC-015: Users can create, rename, reorder, and delete folders, and a folder may contain nested subfolders.
- AC-016: Deleting a folder that contains notes prompts the user to move the notes to another folder or leave them uncategorized.
- AC-017: The sidebar displays a collapsible folder tree.
- AC-018: Users can add multiple tags to a note; tags are reusable, color-coded, searchable, renameable, and removable, and tag names are unique per user ignoring capitalization.
- AC-019: Selecting a tag filters the note list to notes carrying that tag.
- AC-020: A global search field searches note titles and bodies and returns matching notes.
- AC-021: Search results display highlighted matching text where practical.
- AC-022: Search results can be narrowed by folder, tag, date range, note status, and attachment presence.
- AC-023: A keyboard shortcut (Cmd/Ctrl+K) opens global search.
- AC-024: Opening a search result lands the user at the matching content within the note when practical.
- AC-025: Users can pin and unpin a note, and a pinned note remains visually distinct from ordinary notes.
- AC-026: A Pinned filter or dedicated sidebar destination lists pinned notes.
- AC-027: Users can archive a note so it no longer appears in active views but remains retrievable.
- AC-028: Users can move a note to trash, and a trashed note remains recoverable for a documented retention period.
- AC-029: Permanently deleting a note requires explicit confirmation using an unambiguous label such as "Delete permanently" and states that recovery will not be possible.
- AC-030: Restoring a trashed note returns it to its previous folder when that folder still exists, or to the uncategorized note list otherwise, and the application confirms the restoration.
- AC-031: Users can insert checklist items within a note and mark them complete or incomplete without leaving the editor.
- AC-032: A note containing checklist items displays task progress such as "3 of 7 complete."
- AC-033: Notes with at least one unfinished checklist item are filterable as "Open tasks."
- AC-034: Users can attach images, PDFs, text files, and common document formats to a note, and each attachment shows file name, size, upload time, and a download/open control.
- AC-035: An upload exceeding the documented file-size limit, or of an unsupported type, is rejected with a clear error message.
- AC-036: Inline image previews render only for PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP attachments; an SVG attachment is downloadable like other attachments but is never rendered as an inline preview.
- AC-037: A meaningful content change to a note automatically creates a new version in its version history, viewable with timestamps and change previews.
- AC-038: Restoring a prior note version creates a new current version rather than deleting the version history, and the system retains a documented number of versions or a documented retention period.
- AC-039: Users can export an individual note as Markdown, plain text, or PDF.
- AC-040: Users can export their entire note collection as a single portable archive containing Markdown files and attachments.
- AC-041: Initiating a full-collection export requires an explicit confirmation step before the export job starts.
- AC-042: Users can import Markdown or plain-text notes through a review step that reports the number of notes, folders, tags, and attachments that will be created before the import is applied.
- AC-043: Imported Markdown or plain-text content is converted to the same rich-text representation as manually authored notes and passes through the identical allow-list sanitization step before storage.
- AC-044: The note editor accepts Unicode text and content pasted from common browsers and document editors without corrupting the content.
- AC-045: Navigating away from a note while an auto-save request is still pending does not silently discard the pending change: the application either completes the save or warns the user before navigation proceeds.
- AC-046: The note list can be filtered by folder, tag, pinned state, archive state, task-completion state, and date range, independent of any search query.
- AC-047: A note with no title is displayed with a generated label such as "Untitled note" rather than a blank title.
- AC-048: The application records an activity timestamp for each note creation, update, archive, restore, and deletion event.
- AC-049: The desktop layout uses a left navigation sidebar, a central note list, and an optional editor/detail panel.
- AC-050: The mobile layout collapses navigation into a drawer and prioritizes the editor.
- AC-051: Keyboard navigation supports creating a new note, moving through the note list, and predictable focus transitions when saving, in addition to opening search.
- AC-052: The interface provides semantic controls, visible focus states, sufficient color contrast, screen-reader labels, and keyboard-operable navigation throughout.
- AC-053: Account passwords are never stored in plaintext.
- AC-054: An attachment download is served from private object storage that enforces an authorization check before the file is returned.
- AC-055: All client-server traffic is served over HTTPS.
- AC-056: Error messages shown to the user are actionable and do not expose sensitive implementation details such as stack traces, internal identifiers, or raw exception text.
- AC-057: A Trash view lists all trashed notes, from which a user can select a note to restore or permanently delete.
- AC-058: Search results for a collection of up to 10,000 notes per user are returned within approximately one second.

## Out of scope

- Full team collaboration, commenting, and workspace administration.
- Advanced document layout comparable to desktop word processors.
- Native offline-first mobile apps.
- Full project-management features such as sprint planning, dependencies, or Gantt charts.
- Public publishing or external-facing knowledge bases.
- Google sign-in and any authentication method beyond email/password.
- Regular backup/restoration procedures, sub-200ms UI responsiveness targets, and specific browser/version support commitments: the PRD states these as soft, operational-level expectations without a fixed, independently checkable threshold, so this specification leaves them as open operational goals rather than acceptance criteria.
- Access-control treatment for the full-collection export archive, content-type/content-disposition handling for non-image attachment downloads, and password-reset token security properties (expiration, single-use enforcement, rate limiting): the PRD does not decide these, and they should be resolved at the design stage rather than assumed here.
- Further decomposition of compound acceptance criteria (AC-006, AC-009, AC-018, AC-034) into separate sub-behavior IDs: the PRD states each of these as a single feature bullet, so this specification keeps them bundled rather than manufacturing finer-grained obligations the PRD did not separately state.

# Note Keeper — Specification

## Summary

Note Keeper is a web application for individuals to capture, organize, search, and revisit notes, per the Note Keeper product requirements document. This specification covers the full MVP surface described there: authentication, note authoring with sanitized rich text, a dashboard, nested folders, tags, full-text search, pinning, archive/trash with recovery, checklists, attachments, version history, and export/import.

The PRD does not mandate a technology stack or repository layout. The declared artifacts below assume one plausible structure — a TypeScript HTTP backend under `server/` and a React frontend under `client/` — as a basis for delivery. These paths are binding for this specification: delivery is proven by the exact committed paths declared below. If an implementer later needs a different structure, that requires revising this specification's declared-artifacts section, not silently diverging from it.

Where the PRD gives an illustrative number rather than a fixed rule (the attachment file-size limit, and the trash/version retention windows), the acceptance criteria below require that limit or window to be documented and consistently enforced rather than fixing it at the PRD's example value.

The PRD also states several expectations as soft, operational guidance rather than crisp, independently testable, per-artifact obligations: regular backups with a restoration procedure, sub-200ms UI responsiveness "where network conditions allow," and support for "current versions of major browsers." These are intentionally not translated into acceptance criteria below; they are recorded under Out of scope as open operational commitments rather than decided here.

This specification also leaves three security-relevant decisions to the design stage rather than inventing obligations the PRD does not state: access-control treatment for full-collection export archives (which aggregate a user's entire note and attachment set into one artifact), content-type and content-disposition handling for non-image attachment downloads, and password-reset token security properties (expiration, single-use enforcement, enumeration resistance). See Out of scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC-001: Users can register an account with email and password, sign in, sign out, and reset a forgotten password.
- AC-002: A signed-in user can access only their own notes, folders, tags, attachments, and preferences; a request for another user's resource is rejected.
- AC-003: Account passwords are stored only as salted password hashes, never in plaintext.
- AC-004: Clicking "New note" or invoking the note-creation keyboard shortcut opens the editor with the cursor focused in the title or body field.
- AC-005: A note supports a title, body, optional folder assignment, tags, pinned state, archived state, and checklist items.
- AC-006: The editor supports headings, bold, italic, bulleted lists, numbered lists, checklists, links, block quotes, and code blocks.
- AC-007: Edits to a note are auto-saved after a debounce interval of 500-1,000 milliseconds of no typing, without any manual save action.
- AC-008: The editor shows a visible save-state indicator with the states Saving, Saved, Offline, and Unable to save.
- AC-009: Rich-text content is sanitized server-side against a fixed allow-list of tags and attributes matching the supported formatting, both before storage and before rendering, stripping disallowed tags, attributes, inline event handlers, and script content rather than escaping them.
- AC-010: Link and image URLs in rich-text content are restricted to the http, https, and mailto schemes during sanitization; a URL using any other scheme, including javascript: and data:, is rejected.
- AC-011: The dashboard displays recent notes and pinned notes, and each note card or row shows title, content preview, tags, folder, and last-updated timestamp.
- AC-012: Notes can be sorted by last-updated date, creation date, title, or pinned status.
- AC-013: When a user has no notes, the dashboard shows an empty state that guides them to create their first note.
- AC-014: Users can create, rename, reorder, and delete folders, and a folder may contain nested subfolders.
- AC-015: Deleting a folder that contains notes prompts the user to move the contained notes to another folder or leave them uncategorized.
- AC-016: The sidebar displays a collapsible folder tree.
- AC-017: Users can add multiple tags to a note; tags are reusable, color-coded, searchable, renameable, and removable, and tag names are unique per user ignoring capitalization.
- AC-018: Selecting a tag filters the note list to notes carrying that tag.
- AC-019: A global search field searches note titles and bodies and returns results within approximately one second for a collection of up to 10,000 notes for a single user.
- AC-020: Search results can be narrowed by folder, tag, date range, note status, and attachment presence.
- AC-021: A keyboard shortcut (Cmd/Ctrl+K) opens global search.
- AC-022: Search results display highlighted matching text where practical.
- AC-023: Opening a search result lands the user at the matching content within the note when practical.
- AC-024: Users can pin and unpin a note; a pinned note remains visually distinct from ordinary notes and is reachable through a Pinned filter or dedicated sidebar destination.
- AC-025: Users can archive a note so that it no longer appears in active views but remains retrievable.
- AC-026: Users can move a note to trash, and a trashed note remains recoverable for a documented retention period.
- AC-027: Permanently deleting a note requires explicit confirmation using an unambiguous label such as "Delete permanently" and states that the action cannot be undone.
- AC-028: Restoring a trashed note returns it to its previous folder when that folder still exists, or to the uncategorized note list otherwise, and the application confirms the restoration.
- AC-029: Users can insert checklist items within a note and mark them complete without leaving the editor.
- AC-030: A note containing checklist items displays task progress such as "3 of 7 complete," and notes with unfinished checklist items are filterable as "Open tasks."
- AC-031: Users can attach images, PDFs, text files, and common document formats to a note, and each attachment displays its file name, size, upload time, and a download/open control.
- AC-032: An upload that exceeds the documented file-size limit, or that is of an unsupported type, is rejected with a clear error message.
- AC-033: Inline image previews render only for PNG, JPEG, GIF, and WebP attachments; an SVG attachment is downloadable like any other attachment but is never rendered as an inline preview.
- AC-034: A meaningful content change to a note automatically creates a new entry in its version history.
- AC-035: Users can view a note's version history with timestamps and a change preview for each version.
- AC-036: Restoring a prior note version creates a new current version rather than deleting the version history, and the system retains a documented number of versions or a documented retention period.
- AC-037: Users can export an individual note as Markdown, plain text, or PDF.
- AC-038: Users can export their entire note collection as a single portable archive containing Markdown files and attachments.
- AC-039: Users can import Markdown or plain-text notes through a review step that reports the number of notes, folders, tags, and attachments that will be created before the import is applied.
- AC-040: Imported Markdown or plain-text content is converted to the same rich-text representation as manually authored notes and passes through the identical allow-list sanitization step before storage.
- AC-041: A note with no title displays a generated label such as "Untitled note" rather than a blank title.
- AC-042: Navigating away from a note while an auto-save request is still pending does not silently discard the pending change: the application either completes the save first or warns the user before navigation proceeds.
- AC-043: The note editor accepts Unicode text and content pasted from common browsers and document editors without corruption or rejection.
- AC-044: The note list can be filtered by folder, tag, pinned state, archive state, task-completion state, and date range, independent of any search query.
- AC-045: The application records an activity timestamp for each note creation, update, archive, restore, and deletion event.
- AC-046: Exporting the entire note collection requires an explicit confirmation step before the export job starts.
- AC-047: Keyboard navigation supports creating a new note, moving through the note list, and predictable focus transitions when saving, in addition to opening search.
- AC-048: The interface provides semantic controls, visible focus states, sufficient color contrast, screen-reader labels, and keyboard-operable navigation throughout.
- AC-049: All client-server traffic is served over HTTPS.
- AC-050: An attachment download is served from private object storage that enforces an authorization check before the file is returned.
- AC-051: Error messages shown to the user are actionable and do not expose sensitive implementation details such as stack traces, internal identifiers, or raw exception text.
- AC-052: The core workflow of creating, editing, organizing, and finding a note is fully usable on both a desktop browser layout and a mobile browser layout.
- AC-053: Search results are ordered by a combination of relevance and recency rather than an arbitrary or storage order.
- AC-054: Pinned notes appear above unpinned notes in the dashboard and in folder note-list views.
- AC-055: The desktop layout presents a left navigation sidebar, a central note list, and an optional editor/detail panel.
- AC-056: The mobile layout collapses primary navigation into a drawer and prioritizes the note editor.
- AC-057: Destructive actions elsewhere in the interface, such as permanently deleting a folder or removing a tag, use explicit, unambiguous labels rather than generic labels such as "OK."

## Out of scope

- Full team collaboration, commenting, and workspace administration.
- Advanced document layout comparable to desktop word processors.
- Native offline-first mobile apps.

- AC-047: Keyboard navigation supports creating a new note, moving through the note list, and predictable focus transitions when saving, in addition to opening search.
- AC-048: The interface provides semantic controls, visible focus states, sufficient color contrast, screen-reader labels, and keyboard-operable navigation throughout.
- AC-049: All client-server traffic is served over HTTPS.
- AC-050: An attachment download is served from private object storage that enforces an authorization check before the file is returned.
- AC-051: Error messages shown to the user are actionable and do not expose sensitive implementation details such as stack traces, internal identifiers, or raw exception text.
- AC-052: The core workflow of creating, editing, organizing, and finding a note is fully usable on both a desktop browser layout and a mobile browser layout.
- AC-053: Search results are ordered by a combination of relevance and recency rather than an arbitrary or storage order.
- AC-054: Pinned notes appear above unpinned notes in the dashboard and in folder note-list views.
- AC-055: The desktop layout presents a left navigation sidebar, a central note list, and an optional editor/detail panel.
- AC-056: The mobile layout collapses primary navigation into a drawer and prioritizes the note editor.
- AC-057: Destructive actions elsewhere in the interface, such as permanently deleting a folder or removing a tag, use explicit, unambiguous labels rather than generic labels such as "OK."

## Out of scope

- Full team collaboration, commenting, and workspace administration.
- Advanced document layout comparable to desktop word processors.
- Native offline-first mobile apps.
- Full project-management features such as sprint planning, dependencies, or Gantt charts.
- Public publishing or external-facing knowledge bases.
- Google sign-in and any authentication method beyond email/password.
- Regular backup/restoration procedures, sub-200ms UI responsiveness targets, and specific browser/version compatibility guarantees: the PRD states these as soft, operational-level expectations rather than discrete, independently testable per-artifact obligations, and this specification leaves them undecided rather than converting them into acceptance criteria.
- Access-control treatment for full-collection export archives, content-type/content-disposition handling for non-image attachment downloads, and password-reset token security properties (expiration, single-use enforcement, enumeration resistance): the PRD does not decide these, and they are referred to the design stage rather than resolved here.
- User preference/settings behavior beyond the per-user ownership scoping already covered by AC-002 (the PRD's `User.settings` field and its references to account "preferences"): the PRD never defines what preference-setting behavior is required, so no further acceptance criterion or declared artifact is derived from it here.
- The PRD's subjective UX/design language — the overall design feeling "calm, focused, and lightweight," and the editor being "readable, with generous line height and restrained formatting controls" — is not decomposed into acceptance criteria for the same reason as the other soft UX expectations above: it states an aesthetic and comfort goal rather than an independently testable, per-artifact obligation.
